A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T2DA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison. The Humanoid experiment moves from Appendix G in v3 to Appendix I in v5.

before.justification: v3 reports original zero-shot policy evaluations, ablations and robustness experiments on Point-Robot, MuJoCo, Meta-World and Humanoid.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds goal-informed baseline comparisons, instruction-style experiments and additional offline meta-RL comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation (4) changes the normalization used in the stated contrastive objective, affecting the loss in Equation (5). The three training stages, LoRA and both policy architectures are retained. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds Point-Robot scenarios using noisy and conversational instructions, extending language-input coverage beyond the original structured descriptions. The physical tasks and benchmark environments, including Humanoid, are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix J evaluates three additional, closely related comparators: Meta-DT, MetaDiffuser and Prompt-DT, across Point-Robot, Cheetah-Vel and Ant-Dir. This substantially expands the offline meta-RL comparison. The original main and Humanoid comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces goal-augmented observations for baseline comparisons; Appendix H introduces alternate instruction templates with rounded coordinates. Existing splits and training budgets remain unchanged. G's assertion that goal augmentation applies throughout is not reconciled with the differing scores in Tables 1 and 10.

E4.justification: New Appendices G and H examine access to task information and robustness to instruction wording. These are targeted additions; the existing component ablations, data-quality and encoder studies, LoRA comparison and modular-training analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals in Section 4. Added tables continue the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; the modular-training and Humanoid tables retain point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 10, 11 and 13 substantially expand the reported comparison evidence. Ant-Dir results now include Meta-DT at 922.1 alongside retained T2DA-T at 970.3 and T2DA-D at 570.6. Point-Robot reports -7.6 and -8.0 for noisy and conversational instructions, respectively, alongside -7.2 for standard instructions. Original main and Humanoid results are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (4) corrects the probability definitions: denominators sum similarities against a fixed trajectory or text anchor instead of summing only matched pairs. This is a substantive mathematical correction. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamics-aware embeddings, contrastive language-decision alignment, scalable diffuser/transformer implementations and zero-shot generalization.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets goal augmentation as equalizing task-information access, while H interprets its results as robustness and knowledge transfer across instruction styles. Appendix K largely repeats the existing lightweight-data and future real-robot limitations.

D1.justification: v5 adds an implementation-access link in the abstract and states that supplementary source code is provided. Appendix H supplies the additional instruction templates. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v5 adds memory-based RL positioning through RL2 and LLIRL, recent language-model and in-context RL citations, and descriptions of the additional comparators in Appendix C. The central positioning of natural-language supervision relative to context-based adaptation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. v5 corrects wording and the unresolved appendix reference, updates author information, and adds acknowledgements, appendix navigation, additional appendix sections and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The switch to the narrower NeurIPS format changes typography, text wrapping and the placement and sizing of figures, tables and algorithms throughout. Three result tables are added, captions are expanded, and retained displays are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens the evidence with closely related offline meta-RL comparators and targeted language-robustness tests, corrects Equation (4), and adds code-access information. These gains are limited by unresolved protocol clarity: Appendix G does not reconcile its global goal-information assertion with Tables 1 and 10, and H does not clearly distinguish training-time from test-time use of the alternate instructions.
